# Generated piece: petstore

Generated by openapi2piece 0.1.0. Source title: "Synthetic Pet Store".

Run `npm install --ignore-scripts`, then `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build`. Commit the resulting package-lock.json for deployment. Keep the generated compatibility overrides in your installation root (npm ignores dependency-package overrides). The generator itself never installs dependencies or calls the API.

Set Base URL in each action; absolute HTTP(S) only. Requests use a 30-second timeout, no retries, no redirects and no environment proxies. Responses return the parsed body; non-2xx statuses raise a status-only error. Supply connections in the Activepieces 0.32.0 shape (SecretText uses `secret_text`, CustomAuth uses `props`).

Authentication: apiKey. Mixed schemes use optional visible text fields in CustomAuth for compatibility with the pinned metadata validator; use a private connection editor. Each action validates its required credentials. For single-scheme OR alternatives, the required Authentication dropdown (auth_scheme) selects the exact scheme name with no default. If any alternative is an AND group or anonymous ({}), Authentication requirement (auth_requirement) instead selects a canonical JSON string of sorted scheme names, such as ["HeaderKey","QueryKey"]. All credentials in the selected protected group are required and only those credentials are sent. Anonymous uses the canonical value [] and sends no credentials, even with a populated connection. Such actions have requireAuth: false so they can execute without a connection; protected selections still validate every credential locally. Missing/invalid choices or credentials fail before HTTP. There is no automatic fallback, including after HTTP errors. Schemes can be shared across groups; credential collisions are checked within each group. Duplicate scheme sets (including OAuth scope variants), invalid groups and more than 16 alternatives skip the whole operation with reasons. A mixed OAuth2 field is a manually supplied access token without automatic refresh. A lone OAuth2 scheme uses the authorization-code flow and the union of scopes required by generated actions. Anonymous actions send no credentials.

See report.json for every generated and skipped operation and naming warnings. Only scalar path/query/header parameters and single-media JSON request bodies are supported. JSON objects/arrays and oneOf alternatives are validated recursively. OpenAPI 3.0 JSON body schemas exclude readOnly object properties and their same-level required entries recursively through objects, array items and typed additionalProperties. Supply writable fields only, including writeOnly fields with their original constraints. Explicit read-only fields fail before HTTP with a property path such as body.items[0].id; they are never silently stripped. Shared source and response definitions are unchanged, and successful responses are returned intact. Both readOnly and writeOnly true is a schema error. Projection does not extend to composition, root/item annotations, parameters or OpenAPI 3.1 read-only fields; unsupported cases retain report reasons. A oneOf value must match exactly one branch, including for null; invalid or overlapping values fail before HTTP. An explicit type: object wrapper can also require properties and constrain properties/additionalProperties; it must pass independently of the branches. Explicit nullable object wrappers support OpenAPI 3.0 type: object with nullable: true and OpenAPI 3.1 exact type: ["object", "null"] in either order, keeping Object controls; null must satisfy the wrapper and exactly one complete branch, and nullability never bypasses branch matching. An explicit type: string wrapper supports scalar enum and minLength/maxLength (Unicode code points) and must also pass independently of exactly-one branch validation. String wrapper enums stay separate from branch enums and keep a string control without coercion. Explicit type: number/integer wrappers support scalar enum, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum and exclusiveMaximum, independently of exactly-one branches. Wrapper enums remain separate from branch enums and keep a numeric control. OpenAPI 3.0 boolean exclusive bounds use minimum/maximum; 3.1 numeric exclusive bounds are supported. Integer wrappers reject fractions, and numeric inputs are sent as JSON numbers without coercion. Explicit type: array wrappers support items, minItems, maxItems and boolean uniqueItems and require a supported item schema. Wrapper items and bounds are validated independently of exactly-one branches; submitted arrays are sent unchanged without item coercion. uniqueItems: true rejects structurally equal JSON values before HTTP; false or omission permits duplicates. Object key order is irrelevant, array order matters, and booleans, numbers and strings stay distinct (0 equals -0). Wrapper and branch uniqueness remain independent, with no deduplication or branch-enum merging. Finite-number checks and depth 40 still apply. Equality traversal, string/key lengths, key sorting and open JSON traversal share the 100,000-step validation budget per property; exhaustion fails with Input validation limit exceeded before HTTP. Explicit type: boolean wrappers support scalar enum independently of exactly-one complete branches and retain Checkbox controls. true and false are sent unchanged as JSON booleans; required false is present when permitted by the wrapper and branches. Explicit nullable boolean wrappers support OpenAPI 3.0 type: boolean with nullable: true and OpenAPI 3.1 type: ["boolean", "null"] in either order, keeping Checkbox controls. true and null are sent unchanged only when the independent wrapper enum and exactly one complete branch accept them. An enum without null excludes null. Zero complete null matches and duplicate nullable/null matches fail before HTTP; nullability never bypasses branch validation. Type arrays with duplicate entries are rejected during generation, including in complete branches and nested schemas. Required false still passes when permitted. Strings, numbers and missing required values fail locally, with no coercion or enum merging. Explicit nullable string wrappers support OpenAPI 3.0 type: string with nullable: true and OpenAPI 3.1 exact type: ["string", "null"] in either order, keeping ShortText controls. Independent wrapper enum and Unicode code-point minLength/maxLength must pass along with exactly one complete branch, including for null. abc and null are sent unchanged when permitted; enum without null independently excludes null in wrapper or branch. Zero or duplicate complete null matches, missing required values and other JSON types fail before HTTP. Required empty string passes only when enum, length and exactly one branch permit it. No coercion or enum/constraint merging occurs. Explicit nullable number/integer wrappers support OpenAPI 3.0 type: number/integer with nullable: true and OpenAPI 3.1 exact numeric/null type pairs in either order, keeping Number controls. Wrapper enum and minimum/maximum/exclusive bounds remain independent of every complete branch. 1 and null pass unchanged only when the wrapper and exactly one complete branch accept them; enums without null independently exclude it. Zero/duplicate null matches fail before HTTP. Required 0 passes when permitted; integer fractions, nonfinite numbers, booleans, strings and missing required values fail without coercion. Numeric enum schema members must be finite, including direct library inputs. Explicit nullable array wrappers support OpenAPI 3.0 type: array with nullable: true and OpenAPI 3.1 exact type: ["array", "null"] in either order, keeping Array controls with properties: {}. A supported items schema is required even for null-only branches. Wrapper items, minItems/maxItems and boolean uniqueItems remain independent of every complete branch. [0,1] and null are sent unchanged only when the wrapper and exactly one complete branch accept them. [1] fails wrapper minItems, [0,0] fails wrapper uniqueness, [-1,0] fails wrapper items and [0,2] fails its complete array branch in the nullable-array example. Null with zero or duplicate complete matches fails before HTTP; nullable never bypasses branch validation. Required [] passes only when wrapper length and exactly one complete branch permit it. Missing values and wrong types fail without coercion, mutation, deduplication or merging. Other validation siblings, including object/array wrapper enum and cross-type keywords such as minLength on an object wrapper, remain unsupported with report reasons. Incompatible top-level alternatives are skipped in report.json. Relative server URLs require the full absolute API base URL from the action user; their path is not appended. String format is descriptive, and schema defaults/examples are not copied. No triggers, pagination or publishing. Review API semantics, credentials, logoUrl and authors before installing into Activepieces.
